# Family Filter TV — full text

> Family Filter TV is a profanity filter for Android TV, Android TV boxes and Android phones that automatically mutes unwanted language while the picture keeps playing.

Official site: https://familyfiltertv.com/
Short version: https://familyfiltertv.com/llms.txt
Last updated 13 October 2026

# The facts (https://familyfiltertv.com/facts.html)

## What it is
- Name: Family Filter TV (also written FamilyFilterTV)
- In one sentence: A profanity filter for Android TV, Android TV boxes and Android phones that automatically mutes unwanted language while the picture keeps playing.
- Website: https://familyfiltertv.com/
- Filter levels: Off, mild, family or strict. The filter is set once on a parent's phone and every linked device follows it.

## What it does
- Mutes profanity in speech. Only the sound drops, for the length of that line, and then comes straight back.
- Works with supported playback you start in Stremio.
- Follows along while you watch Netflix and other apps on an Android TV or Google TV: you pick the same title on an Android phone and the TV mutes the swearing. It needs version 0.2.21 or newer, English titles only for now. Muting is best effort, so a line may slip through. Family Filter TV is not affiliated with Netflix.
- Links a television by the short code it shows on screen, typed into the phone app.
- Has an early-beta companion for Windows 10 and 11 that mutes the computer's sound while a flagged word is spoken.

## What it does not do
- It does not filter violence or nudity.
- It does not cut, skip or blur the video.
- It is not a streaming library and does not provide films, series or subscription access.
- It only mutes when subtitles are found for the title. Filtering availability varies by title, and the app tells the viewer when filtering is unavailable.
- It does not work with the built-in apps of Samsung (Tizen), LG (webOS), Hisense VIDAA and other non-Android TVs. Roku TVs and Amazon Fire TV are not supported at this time.
- It does not filter DStv.

## Where it runs
- Runs on: Android TVs and Android TV boxes (including Google TV), Android phones, and Windows 10 or 11 as an early beta.
- Does not run on: The built-in apps of Samsung and LG TVs, Hisense sets running VIDAA, Roku TVs and Amazon Fire TV. A Google TV or Android TV streaming stick or box plugged into the TV's HDMI port works.
- How to tell: Press Home on the TV remote. If you see Google TV, or the Google Play Store among the apps, it works. See https://familyfiltertv.com/which-tvs.html .

## What you need
- A Family Filter TV account.
- An Android phone (Android 7.0 or newer) with the Family Filter TV app.
- Subtitles for the film or episode.
- For follow along in Netflix and other apps: Family Filter TV on an Android TV or Google TV device and on an Android phone.

## Versions and where to get them
- Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.familyfiltertv.app (package com.familyfiltertv.app).
- Direct install (APK): For TV boxes without Google Play. The current version is on https://familyfiltertv.com/download.html .
- Follow along needs: Version 0.2.21 or newer. If Google Play still offers an older version, install from https://familyfiltertv.com/download.html .
- Windows: Early beta for Windows 10 and 11. See https://familyfiltertv.com/download.html#windows .
- Language Ratings: A separate, free Stremio add-on that counts the swearing in a film from its English subtitles. It only counts; it does not mute. See https://familyfiltertv.com/stremio.html .

## Price
- Annual price: US$14.99 a year, with the first 14 days free. Google Play shows and charges the price in your own currency.
- Devices: Three devices are included on one account, and up to six can be linked. A 4th, 5th or 6th device adds US$3.09, US$5.99 or US$8.99 a year.
- Inviting friends: Every friend who subscribes through your link earns you 10 weeks free. Your friend gets 30 days free instead of the usual 14.

## Who makes it
- Made by: Jacques du Preez, in South Africa.
- Contact: jacquesjdupreez@gmail.com
- Channels: YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@FamilyFilterTV , Instagram https://www.instagram.com/familyfiltertv/ , TikTok https://www.tiktok.com/@familyfiltertvapp
- Not affiliated: Family Filter TV is an independent app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Stremio, Netflix, Google, OpenSubtitles or any streaming service.

# Questions and answers from the site

## Home page (https://familyfiltertv.com/)

Q: What happens if a title has no subtitles?
A: Filtering availability varies by title. Family Filter TV tells you on screen when filtering is unavailable.

Q: Does it cut or skip anything?
A: No. Only the sound drops, and only for the length of that line.

Q: Which devices does it run on?
A: The television itself — Android TVs and TV boxes — and Android phones. A few TV boxes don't offer the Play Store at all; install it directly on those. There's also an early-beta companion for Windows PCs.

Q: What does it play?
A: Nothing itself. It filters supported playback you start in Stremio, and it can follow along while you watch Netflix and other apps on your Android TV. Family Filter TV is not a streaming library and does not provide access to subscription services.

Q: Does it work with Netflix?
A: Yes, on Android TV and Google TV. Start the episode or film in Netflix on the TV, pick the same title in Family Filter TV on your phone, and the TV mutes the swearing as you watch. When the TV cannot tell where you are in the film, the phone can find the place by listening; the sound is turned into words on the phone only and is never stored or sent. See the quick start. Family Filter TV is not affiliated with Netflix.

Q: Does it do anything about violence or nudity?
A: No. It mutes swearing in speech and nothing else. Nothing is blurred, cut or skipped.

Q: Is there a launch discount?
A: It starts 1 October 2026. The first 200 subscribers in South Africa and the first 200 elsewhere get 50% off their first year, stepping down to 40%, 30%, 20% and 10% as each group of 200 fills, until 31 December 2026. After that it's the full price.

Q: How does inviting a friend work?
A: Every friend who subscribes through your link earns you 10 weeks free, credited 3 days after their first payment. Five friends is a free year, and there's no cap after that. Your friend gets 30 days free instead of the usual 14 and pays their own subscription, at the launch price while it lasts.

Q: Does one setting cover every television in the house?
A: Yes. The filter belongs to the household, not to the device. You set it on your phone and every linked television follows. A television is linked by typing in the short code it shows on screen. Three devices are included on one account, and up to six can be linked.

Q: What does Family Filter TV cost?
A: US$14.99 a year, with the first 14 days free. Google Play shows and charges the price in your own currency. One account covers three devices, and more can be added up to six.

Q: Will it work on my TV?
A: It depends on the system your TV runs, not the brand. If your TV has the Google Play Store, yes. Which TVs has the brand-by-brand answer.

Q: Something isn't working.
A: Support has the setup steps, the known limits, and an address to write to.

## Profanity filter for Android TV: how it works and what it can't do (https://familyfiltertv.com/profanity-filter-android-tv.html)

Q: How does a profanity filter on Android TV actually work?
A: Family Filter TV reads the subtitle track of whatever's playing in Stremio. A matching line mutes the audio for its length, then sound returns automatically. The picture keeps playing throughout.

Q: Does it need subtitles to work?
A: Yes — filtering depends on a subtitle track existing for that title. Without one, the app tells you filtering isn't available rather than guessing.

Q: Does it filter violence or nudity on Android TV?
A: No. It filters spoken profanity only. Nothing is blurred, cut or skipped.

Q: Does it work with Netflix or DStv on Android TV?
A: Netflix, yes on Android TV and Google TV, through follow mode: pick the title on your Android phone and the TV mutes the swearing. It also works with supported playback started in Stremio. DStv is not supported, and Family Filter TV isn't affiliated with Netflix or any other streaming service.

Q: What Android TV devices does it run on?
A: Android TVs, Android TV boxes, and Android phones — the app itself, no computer needed.

Q: Can one setting cover every TV in the house?
A: Yes. Set the filter strength once on a phone and every linked television follows it.

## Mute swearing in Stremio: step-by-step (https://familyfiltertv.com/stremio-profanity-filter.html)

Q: Does Stremio have a profanity filter?
A: No. There is no setting for it anywhere in Stremio. Family Filter TV adds it as a separate app that plays alongside Stremio as the external player, muting profanity while the picture keeps playing.

Q: How do I mute swearing in Stremio on Android TV?
A: Install Stremio and Family Filter TV on the same Android TV or TV box, link the TV from the Family Filter TV phone app with the short code, choose a filter strength, and set Family Filter TV as the external player in Stremio's Player menu. Make sure the title has English subtitles.

Q: Why is nothing being muted?
A: Check that Stremio's Player menu is still set to External, Family Filter TV, because Android can reset an app's default after an update. Also check that the release you picked has an English subtitle track. Without subtitles there is nothing to read, and Family Filter TV says so on screen.

Q: Does it filter violence or nudity?
A: No. It filters spoken profanity only. Violence and nudity are not currently filtered.

## Mute swearing on TV without cutting the video (https://familyfiltertv.com/mute-swearing-on-tv.html)

Q: How do you mute swearing on TV without cutting the video?
A: Use an app that listens for swear words and lowers the sound for a moment. Family Filter TV does this on Android TV, Google TV and Android TV boxes: unwanted language is automatically muted when filtering is available, the sound returns by itself, and the picture keeps playing.

Q: Does it cut or skip scenes?
A: No. The picture keeps playing normally and nothing is cut, blurred or skipped. Only the sound briefly drops.

Q: Which TVs does it work on?
A: Android TV, Google TV and Android TV boxes, with a companion app on an Android phone. It does not work with the built-in apps of Samsung, LG and other non-Android TVs.

Q: Can it mute swearing on Netflix?
A: Family Filter TV follows along while you watch Netflix and other apps on your Android TV or Google TV: you pick the title on your Android phone and the TV mutes the swearing. Muting is best effort and works for English titles for now. Family Filter TV is not affiliated with Netflix.

Q: Does it filter violence or nudity?
A: No. Its focus today is unwanted language, and it does not filter violence or nudity.

## How to mute swearing on Netflix (https://familyfiltertv.com/mute-swearing-on-netflix.html)

Q: Can you mute swearing on Netflix on a TV?
A: Yes, on an Android TV or Google TV. Family Filter TV runs on the TV next to the Netflix app and mutes the sound for the swear words it finds in the subtitles, while the picture keeps playing. Muting is best effort, so a line may slip through. Family Filter TV is not affiliated with Netflix.

Q: Does it work on Samsung or LG TVs?
A: Not with the Netflix app built into Samsung, LG and other non-Android TVs. It works on Android TV and Google TV sets and boxes.

Q: Do browser extensions that filter Netflix work on a TV?
A: No. Browser extensions run in a web browser on a computer. They do not run inside the Netflix app on a TV.

Q: Does Family Filter TV change Netflix or the video?
A: No. It does not change the Netflix app, cut scenes or provide any films or series. You watch with your own Netflix account, and Family Filter TV only lowers the TV sound for a moment.

## Does Netflix have a profanity filter? (https://familyfiltertv.com/does-netflix-have-a-profanity-filter.html)

Q: Does Netflix have a profanity filter?
A: No. Netflix has parental controls that decide which titles a profile can see, but we found no Netflix setting that mutes or bleeps swearing inside a title. To mute swearing while the picture keeps playing, you need a separate tool.

Q: Can I mute swearing on Netflix on my TV?
A: Yes, on an Android TV or Google TV. Family Filter TV runs on the TV next to the Netflix app and mutes the sound for the swear words it finds in the subtitles, while the picture keeps playing. Muting is best effort, so a line may slip through. Family Filter TV is not affiliated with Netflix.

Q: Do Netflix Kids profiles remove swearing?
A: A Kids profile limits the maturity level of the titles it shows. It does not edit the audio of a title, so it is a way to choose what appears, not a way to mute words.

Q: Do browser extensions that filter Netflix work on a TV?
A: No. Browser extensions run in a web browser on a computer. They do not run inside the Netflix app on a TV.

Q: Does Family Filter TV filter violence or nudity on Netflix?
A: No. Family Filter TV mutes spoken profanity only. It does not filter violence or nudity, and it works for English titles for now.


## Swearing in movies (https://familyfiltertv.com/swearing-in-movies.html)

Q: When was swearing first allowed in Hollywood movies?
A: Not until the late 1960s. The Production Code, in force from 1934 to 1968, banned profanity in American studio films, with rare exceptions such as the word damn in Gone with the Wind (1939), which producer David O. Selznick won an exemption for. The ratings system that replaced the Code on 1 November 1968 let studios release films with stronger language, marked by their rating.

Q: What was the first movie to use the F-word?
A: It depends on what counts. Director Robert Altman said M*A*S*H (1970) was the first major American studio film to use the word, and the Wikipedia list of films that most use it describes M*A*S*H as the first mainstream American film under the ratings system to do so. Films from outside the major studios and from other countries may have used the word earlier.

Q: Which movie has the most swearing?
A: By reported count of the F-word, Swearnet: The Movie (2014) leads with 935, and the documentary Fuck (2005) follows with 857. Among narrative feature films, The Wolf of Wall Street (2013) is listed at 569, though sources give between 506 and 569. In our own subtitle analysis of 1,286 films, the heaviest has 837 flagged words of all kinds.

Q: How much swearing is normal in a movie?
A: Less than the famous records suggest. In 1,286 films we counted from their English subtitles, half have 43 or fewer flagged words, 4% have none, and about one in four has 100 or more. Flagged words include mild language such as damn and religious exclamations, not only strong profanity.

Q: Can I watch a movie with the swearing muted?
A: On an Android TV or Google TV, yes. Family Filter TV mutes the swear words it finds in the subtitles while the picture keeps playing. It works with supported Stremio playback and follows along with Netflix and other apps. It covers spoken language only, English titles for now, and muting is best effort, so a word may slip through. Family Filter TV is not affiliated with Netflix.

## VidAngel and ClearPlay alternative for Stremio households (https://familyfiltertv.com/vidangel-clearplay-alternative.html)

Q: Does VidAngel work in South Africa?
A: No. VidAngel's own support documentation says it cannot support its service outside the United States, including US military bases and embassies.

Q: Does ClearPlay work in South Africa?
A: No. ClearPlay's help documentation describes it as designed for use in the United States only, with no plans to expand.

Q: What's the difference between VidAngel and ClearPlay?
A: Both filter language, violence and nudity over an existing US streaming subscription. VidAngel connects directly to services like Netflix and Prime Video; ClearPlay is a Chrome extension over services including Amazon, Disney+ and Netflix. Neither is a standalone Android TV app.

Q: Is Family Filter TV a VidAngel or ClearPlay alternative?
A: For a narrower problem: it mutes spoken profanity in Stremio playback on Android TV, TV boxes and phones, anywhere Stremio and subtitles reach, and it can follow along while you watch Netflix and other apps on Android TV or Google TV (English titles only for now). It doesn't filter violence or nudity, muting is best effort, and it doesn't work with DStv.

## Movie filtering services compared (https://familyfiltertv.com/movie-filtering-services-compared.html)

Q: Which movie filtering service is cheapest?
A: On the list prices in the table above, Family Filter TV at US$14.99 a year is the lowest annual price of the paid subscriptions. Enjoy Movies Your Way also has a free plan and lists a premium plan at $7.99 a month, and TVGuardian is a one-off hardware purchase. Prices change, so check each service's own site.

Q: Which of these filter violence and nudity?
A: VidAngel and ClearPlay filter violence and sex or nudity as well as language, and Enjoy Movies Your Way covers violence and other content through tags. Family Filter TV mutes spoken profanity only and does not filter violence or nudity.

Q: Do any of these work outside the United States?
A: VidAngel's support pages and ClearPlay's help documentation both say their services are for use in the United States only. Family Filter TV is not restricted to the United States. The sources we checked did not state a country limit for Enjoy Movies Your Way or TVGuardian, so check their sites.

Q: Which of these run on a TV without a computer?
A: VidAngel and Enjoy Movies Your Way list apps for TV platforms on their own sites. ClearPlay runs as a Chrome extension on a computer that you connect to the TV. TVGuardian is a separate box that reads closed captions. Family Filter TV runs on Android TV and Google TV sets and boxes, with a companion app on an Android phone.

Q: Is Family Filter TV affiliated with any of these services?
A: No. Family Filter TV is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to VidAngel, ClearPlay, Enjoy Movies Your Way, TVGuardian or any streaming service.

## Profanity filter browser extension or television: what is the difference? (https://familyfiltertv.com/profanity-filter-browser-extension-vs-tv.html)

Q: Can a browser extension filter my TV?
A: An extension runs inside the browser where it is installed. Check the extension's own page for any casting instructions; it does not install on apps built into a television.

Q: Does Family Filter TV work in a browser?
A: Not as an extension. For a PC there is an early-beta Windows 10 and 11 companion that mutes the computer's sound for whatever is playing in a browser or app.

Q: Does Family Filter TV filter web page text?

## Family movie night without the swearing (https://familyfiltertv.com/family-movie-night-without-swearing.html)

Q: How can I watch a film without the swearing?
A: You can use an edited version if one exists, use parental controls to pick suitable ratings, watch ahead yourself, or use a filter that mutes spoken profanity. Many families combine two.

Q: Do parental controls remove swearing?
A: No. They block titles by age rating. They do not change the words inside a title you allow.

Q: Does a mute filter cut scenes?
A: No. Family Filter TV mutes the sound for a moment. The picture keeps playing.

Q: Will a filter catch all the swearing?
A: No. It depends on subtitles, and muting is best effort, so a line may slip through. It filters speech only, not violence or nudity.

## Profanity filter for Google TV (https://familyfiltertv.com/google-tv-profanity-filter.html)

Q: Does Family Filter TV work on Google TV?
A: Yes. Google TV runs the same system as Android TV, and Family Filter TV runs on both.

Q: How do I know if my TV is a Google TV?
A: Press Home on the remote. If you see Google TV, or the Google Play Store among the apps, it works.

Q: Does it work on a Google TV streaming stick or box?
A: Yes. Sticks and boxes work the same as a Google TV set. They also give a simple option for a TV that cannot run the app itself.

Q: Do I need a phone?
A: Yes. Install the app on an Android phone too. The phone is where you sign in, link the TV and choose the title to follow.

Q: Will it mute swearing in the Netflix app on Google TV?

## Parental controls vs a profanity filter (https://familyfiltertv.com/parental-controls-vs-profanity-filter.html)

Q: What is the difference between parental controls and a profanity filter?
A: Parental controls block titles by age rating. A profanity filter mutes swear words inside a title you allow.

Q: Do parental controls stop swearing?
A: No. A film that passes the rating limit plays in full, including any swearing.

Q: Does a profanity filter block films?
A: No. Family Filter TV does not block anything. It mutes spoken profanity while the picture keeps playing.

Q: Should I use both?
A: Many families do. Parental controls decide what can start. A filter handles the language in titles you allow.

Q: Does Family Filter TV change Stremio’s settings?
A: No. Stremio’s settings are separate. Family Filter TV works alongside Stremio and is not affiliated with it.

Q: Does a filter also remove violence or nudity?
A: No. Family Filter TV mutes speech only.

## Profanity filter for a Windows PC (https://familyfiltertv.com/windows-profanity-filter.html)

Q: Is there a profanity filter for a Windows PC?
A: Yes, as an early beta. Family Filter TV for Windows mutes the computer’s sound over flagged words while the picture keeps playing. It needs the Family Filter TV phone app on the same account.

Q: Which versions of Windows does it support?
A: Windows 10 and Windows 11.

Q: Why does Windows warn me when I install it?
A: The app is not code-signed yet, so Windows shows a blue “Windows protected your PC” warning. Choose More info, then Run anyway.

Q: Does it work in my browser and in apps?
A: It works with whatever you are watching on the PC, in a browser or an app. It mutes the whole computer’s sound, not one app.

Q: Does it need my phone?
A: Yes. You pick the show and fix the timing on the Family Filter TV phone app. The phone listens to find the place in the film.

Q: Will it catch every swear word?
A: No. It is an early beta and checks the sound only every couple of seconds, so it can miss words. It filters speech only, not violence or nudity.

## Get set up (https://familyfiltertv.com/setup.html)

Q: Does the phone need to listen?
A: Only sometimes. With Netflix on your Android TV, the TV reads where you are in the film by itself, so no listening is needed. In some other apps, on live channels, and on a Windows computer, the TV or computer cannot tell where you are. Then the phone finds the place by listening to the show.

Q: How does listening work?
A: Once you have allowed the microphone, the phone starts listening by itself when you follow a title. It usually lines up within a few seconds of clear talking. It keeps listening while the Follow screen is open, so it can correct itself after a pause or a skip. Tap Stop if you want it to stop.

Q: The phone says it can hardly hear the show
A: Turn the volume up. Or play the sound through speakers instead of headphones, so the phone can hear it.

Q: It will not line up during a song or a quiet scene
A: The phone needs people talking. It cannot line up during songs or scenes with no talking. Give it a moment once the talking starts again.

Q: I would rather type the time
A: Tap Type the time and type the time the player shows. Just type the digits: 10750 becomes 1:07:50, and 750 becomes 7:50.

Q: I locked my phone
A: The phone does not listen while it is locked or the app is in the background. The TV keeps time by itself. If you pause or skip, open the app again so the phone can correct it.

Q: Nothing is being muted
A: Family Filter TV only mutes when it finds the right subtitles, and it tells you when it cannot. Check step 4 of the quick start: on the TV, under Follow along, notification access must say Granted. That is how the TV sees what is playing. Still stuck? Write to us from the support page.

## Install Family Filter TV (https://familyfiltertv.com/install.html)

Q: Does Family Filter TV only work with Stremio?
A: No. It works with Netflix and other apps on your Android TV or Google TV: you follow the title from your phone and the TV mutes the swear words. Stremio is one more way to watch, where the film plays through Family Filter TV directly.

Q: Which should I choose, Google Play or the direct install?
A: Use Google Play if it lists Family Filter TV for your device. If it does not, use the direct install. It is the same app. Pick one per device, because the two cannot be installed over each other.

Q: Is the direct install safe?
A: It is the same app, built from the same source and signed with our key, downloaded from familyfiltertv.com. The page shows a checksum of the file so you can check it.

Q: Do I need both a TV and a phone?
A: Yes. The TV does the muting. The phone is where you sign in, link the TV and choose what you are watching. A Windows computer can stand in for the TV in the early beta.

## Install Family Filter TV on Android TV or Google TV (https://familyfiltertv.com/install-android-tv.html)

Q: Why can't I find Family Filter TV in the Play Store on my TV?
A: Google Play may not list it for your TV yet. Use the direct install with Downloader above. It is the same app and works on any Android TV or Google TV running Android 7.0 or newer.

Q: It says the app was not installed. What now?
A: Almost always a copy from the other route is already on the TV, for example the Google Play version when you are installing directly. The two are signed differently and cannot go over each other. Uninstall Family Filter TV in the TV's Settings, then install again.

Q: Android says unknown apps are blocked.
A: Switch on the unknown apps permission for Downloader, as in step 2 of the direct install. On Android 8 and later it is under Settings, Apps, Special app access, Install unknown apps.

Q: Downloader cannot load the address.
A: Check that the TV is connected to the internet and that you typed familyfiltertv.com/apk exactly, with no spaces and no www.

Q: Does it update itself?
A: The Google Play version updates through the Play Store. The direct version checks for a newer build from its own Settings screen and installs it after you allow unknown apps for the app.

## Install Family Filter TV on an Android phone (https://familyfiltertv.com/install-android-phone.html)

Q: Does it work on an iPhone?
A: No. Family Filter TV is an Android app, and you need an Android phone with Android 7.0 or newer.

Q: Why does the phone ask to use the microphone?
A: In some apps, on live channels and on a Windows computer the TV cannot tell where you are in the show, so the phone listens to find the place. The sound is recognised on the phone and is not saved or sent anywhere. With Netflix on an Android TV the TV reads the place itself and no listening is needed.

Q: Android says it cannot install the app.
A: If you used the direct install, allow installs from unknown apps for the browser or file app you opened it from. If it says the app was not installed, a copy from the Google Play route is probably already on the phone. Uninstall it and try again.

Q: Can the phone and the TV use different routes?
A: Yes. The phone can be on Google Play and the TV on the direct install, or the other way round. Only one route per device.

## Install Family Filter TV on Windows (https://familyfiltertv.com/install-windows.html)

Q: Why does Windows warn me when I run the installer?
A: The Windows app is an early beta and is not code-signed yet, so Windows shows a blue protected-your-PC warning. Choose More info, then Run anyway.

Q: Does the phone have to listen?
A: Yes, on a computer. A computer cannot tell where it is in a film, so the phone listens to the show to find the place. Allow the microphone and keep the phone near the computer's speakers.

Q: Does it mute only the video I am watching?
A: It mutes the whole computer's sound for the moment a flagged word is spoken, then the sound comes back.

## Support (https://familyfiltertv.com/support.html)

Q: How does follow mode work?
A: Follow mode lets Family Filter TV follow along while you watch Netflix and other apps on an Android TV or Google TV. Start the title in the app on the TV, pick the same title in Family Filter TV on your Android phone, and the TV mutes the swearing. When the episode ends, the TV follows the next one by itself. Muting is best effort. The quick start in the setup guide has the five steps.

Q: Does the phone listen to my TV?
A: Only when it has to. With Netflix on your Android TV, the TV reads where you are in the film by itself. When the TV or a Windows computer cannot tell, the phone finds the place by listening. Once you have allowed the microphone, it starts by itself when you follow a title, usually within a few seconds of clear talking, and it keeps listening while the Follow screen is open so it can correct itself after a pause or a skip. Tap Stop to stop it. The sound is turned into words on the phone and compared there with the subtitles. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere. See If it is not in sync and the privacy policy.

Q: What are the limits of follow mode?
A: Needs Family Filter TV on an Android TV or Google TV device and on an Android phone. English titles only for now. Does not work with the built-in apps of Samsung, LG and other non-Android TVs. See Will it work on my TV? Family Filter TV is not affiliated with Netflix.
